It is a trivial problem in terms of managing tex files, because as I
said in the last post there, you can easily separate those parts that
are not relevant to R to individual files, and \input{} them into the
main document.

On Wed, Dec 19, 2012 at 6:31 PM, Ross Ahmed <ross...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> In linked post, the opening poster requests to re-run source code with
> 'compile pdf', without over-writing any changes to the text:
> https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!topic/knitr/FSAI2LM1eGc
>
> My understanding of this scenario is as follows:
> 1. I create a .Rnw file which includes both R code and normal text
> 2. I run 'compile pdf'
> 3. In the resultant .tex file, I and colleagues make various changes to the
> text
> 4. I re-run 'compile pdf', but any changes to the text in the .tex file are
> lost, and the resultant pdf is whatever R code/text is contained in the .Rnw
> file
>
> My understanding of knitr is limited, but surely if text is over-written in
> the .tex file every time 'compile pdf' is run, this creates problems? Is it
> possible to keep the .Rnw file and .tex file in sync with each other so that
> changes in one file, will show in the other file?
